maya: Heads-up — saw a ~7% p95 tail latency regression on streaming routes after last runtime push. Metrics show more KV cache misses + more frequent small-kernel fallbacks. Anyone picked this up on canary?

liam: Yeah, noticed it earlier. Canary shows average batch size for stream-enabled routes dropped from 12.3 -> 6.1. Partial-decode preemption looks like it's cutting coalescing windows short. :eyes:

sanjay: Can you paste the profile or the pprof snippet? Which model family and kernel configs are affected?

maya: Pasted pprof snapshot from host-22 (trimmed):
```
# cpu profile (top)
80.2%  runtime/kernel_small (hot)
10.1%  runtime/kv_miss_handler
6.0%   runtime/partial_decode_scheduler
3.7%   user/decoder
```
Model: rw-large-2.7b-quant. Kernel-selector logs: recent seq_len histogram mean 58 -> 22 after the push.

eva: My hunch: streaming clients doing early-send cause early-flush heuristic to fire, producing many short-lived batches. The batcher then selects the low-latency small kernel which is actually suboptimal for longer continuations (higher per-token cost). Two quick ideas: bump token_budget_floor for streaming sessions (e.g., 3 -> 6) and increase coalesce window by 5-10ms when stream flag present.

liam: Also worth noting: kernel-selector is using a raw histogram built from recent requests. If partial-decodes are overrepresented the histogram skews small and we pick the small kernel globally. Could change aggregator to weight full-decode requests more (e.g., full weight 0.7, partial 0.3) or ignore pure partial-only samples.

infra-bot: Deploy queued: runtime/streaming-fixes #442 will roll to canary group at 2026-03-17T22:12 (CI job triggered).

maya: Plan to run an experiment now: 1) set streaming.token_budget_floor=6 for canary; 2) add ignore_partial flag to kernel_hist aggregator; 3) delay partial-decode preemption by +5ms to favor coalescing. Will run 2h canary and report.

sanjay: Quick caution — increasing the coalesce window can spike KV miss rate during rollout because we re-order request timings. Recommend a synthetic pre-warm step: fire small warmup prompts to populate KV before full traffic shifts.

eva: Also add two observability metrics before the roll: runtime.kernel_fallback_rate and stream.early_flush_count. Create alerts if fallback_rate > 2% over baseline or early_flush_count increases > x10.

maya: Roger. Kicking off canary on 2 hosts (host-22, host-27). Patch/PR: https://git.redwood/infr/runtime/pulls/547 — will post results in ~2h. :thumbsup:
